projects.title: Urban Heat-Island Microclimate Mesh
projects.description: Low-cost solar LoRaWAN sensor nodes paired with shade-canopy routing to alert vulnerable neighborhoods before dangerous urban heat peaks.
projects.targetAudience: Municipal climate planners and elderly residents in dense urban wards
projects.supportingInfo: Pilot ward shows 4.2°C variance between shaded parks and asphalt transit corridors.

problemAnalysis.summary: Dense urban districts lack hyper-local thermal telemetry, causing city cooling centers and shade transit advisories to activate hours after street-level heat stress peaks.
problemAnalysis.refinedStatement: How might municipal health teams capture block-level wet-bulb temperature gradients in real time to dispatch mobile cooling resources before heat-related hospitalizations spike?
rootCauses: Weather stations sit at airports miles away from asphalt-heavy residential corridors
Commercial microclimate sensors cost $1,200+ per node, preventing block-level coverage
Cooling center alerts rely on static daily forecasts rather than real-time pedestrian exposure
stakeholders: Older adults and outdoor transit commuters
Municipal public health & emergency response coordinators
Urban forestry and streetscape planning departments
currentChallenges: Battery degradation inside unshaded solar enclosures above 45°C
Zero-connectivity dead zones along concrete underpasses
Communicating actionable cool-route alerts without smartphone dependency
possibleImpact: Earlier activation of neighborhood cooling hubs during peak afternoon humidity
Empirical street-level heat maps to prioritize urban tree canopy funding
researchQuestions: What node spacing (250m vs 500m) yields reliable interpolation across mixed-height blocks?
How can community pharmacies act as passive LoRaWAN gateway hosts?
missingInformation: Historical ward-level EMS heat dispatch timestamps for baseline validation
Local municipal permitting rules for streetlight pole mounting
opportunities: Combine passive radiative-cooling enclosures with sub-GHz mesh relays
Publish open GeoJSON heat feeds for local transit routing apps

solutions.name: Solar LoRaWAN Mesh + Community Pharmacy Gateways
solutions.shortDescription: Self-powered ESP32-S3 + SHT45 sensor pucks mounted on transit shelters relaying hourly thermal deltas through neighborhood pharmacy gateways.
solutions.workingPrinciple: Sensors wake every 5 minutes, sample temperature, humidity, and solar irradiance, and transmit compressed 18-byte payloads via LoRaWAN to a cloud ingestion pipeline.
advantages: Under $38 bill of materials per street node in small batches
Zero cellular SIM fees via community-hosted gateways
Operates up to 14 days on LiFePO4 reserve without direct sun
limitations: Requires mounting permission from transit authority or local storefronts
risks: Enclosure thermal drift if radiation shield airflow is obstructed

solutions.name: Fleet-Mounted Transit Bus Thermal Probes
solutions.shortDescription: Attach ruggedized thermal-GPS loggers to municipal buses to map street corridors dynamically throughout service hours.
solutions.workingPrinciple: Buses sweep major arterials every 15 minutes, uploading geo-tagged temperature traces over existing onboard cellular routers.
advantages: Instant multi-ward spatial coverage without fixed pole permits
Direct access to reliable 24V vehicle power
limitations: Measures roadway asphalt corridors rather than residential courtyards
Engine heat skews readings at low speeds or idling stops
risks: Transit union and fleet maintenance scheduling delays

solutions.name: Satellite LST + Citizen SMS Micro-Survey
solutions.shortDescription: Downscale Landsat/ECOSTRESS thermal imagery with targeted SMS comfort check-ins from community volunteers.
solutions.workingPrinciple: Combines morning satellite land-surface passes with regression downscaling and hyper-local human comfort reports.
advantages: Zero hardware manufacturing or maintenance overhead
Rapid deployment within a single hackathon weekend
limitations: Cloud cover blocks thermal satellite passes on humid days
Land surface temperature differs significantly from shaded air temperature
risks: Volunteer survey fatigue during multi-day heat waves

roadmapPhases.title: Phase 2: Gateway Mesh & Live Heatmap
roadmapPhases.objective: Connect 5 pilot nodes to a ChirpStack LoRaWAN server and render ward-level heat advisories.
testingRequirements: Packet delivery rate > 96% across 600m urban blocks

pitch.problemStatement: Citywide heat warnings rely on airport weather stations miles away, leaving vulnerable neighborhoods blind to 4°C+ street-level thermal spikes.
pitch.existingLimitations: Commercial environmental stations cost over $1,200 per unit and require cellular contracts, making block-by-block deployment financially impossible.
pitch.proposedSolution: A $38 solar-powered LoRaWAN sensor mesh hosted on neighborhood storefronts, streaming live wet-bulb heat alerts and cool-route maps.
pitch.innovation: Combines ultra-low-power radiative shielding with zero-fee community gateways and automated cooling-center dispatch triggers.
pitch.technologyStack: ESP32-S3, SX1262 LoRaWAN, SHT45, TimescaleDB, MapLibre GL, React + TypeScript
pitch.implementationPlan: Phase 1 calibrates 5 pilot nodes; Phase 2 partners with 3 community pharmacies for gateway hosting; Phase 3 integrates municipal SMS alerts.
pitch.expectedImpact: Gives city health teams 2–3 hours of earlier intervention window and empirical data for targeted shade-tree planting.
pitch.futureScope: Expand telemetry to particulate air-quality indexing (PM2.5) for wildfire smoke events.

sections.heading: Problem Context
sections.content: Airport weather readings routinely underestimate asphalt-corridor street temperatures by 3–5°C, delaying municipal cooling center activations.

sections.heading: Proposed Architecture
sections.content: Deploy $38 solar-powered ESP32-S3 LoRaWAN nodes inside passive radiation shields, routing hyper-local wet-bulb telemetry through community pharmacy gateways.

sections.heading: Next Milestone
sections.content: Finalize 5-node pilot deployment and integrate live GeoJSON heat advisories with local transit routing.
